page.layout: One page of text. At the top, two portrait medallions with legends around them, centred under the running head. Below them, one column of running text in two paragraphs, followed by a gathering signature at the right. An ornament block sits at the foot. No notes in the margins.

main_text.p: ÆLIVS Adrianus, cognomento Afer, Adriani Imperatoris pater fuit, ac Traiani consobrinus: huius origo vetustior à Picentibus, posterior ab Hispanensibus manat: siquidem Adria ortos maiores suos apud Italiam Scipionum temporibus resedisse, in libris vitæ suæ Adrianus ipse commemorat. est autem Adria, seu Hadria, oppidum agri Piceni, quod etiā mari Adriatico nomen dedisse nonnulli censent: attamen huic refragatur opinioni Plin.li.3.cap.16.ab Atria Thuscorum oppido, Atriaticum mare dictum censens, quod post mutatione vnius tantùm literæ Adriaticum dici cæpit. Cæterùm quatenus attinet ad Ælium Adrianum, vide Ælium Spartianum, & Sex. Aurelium Victorem. Sunt qui Hadrianum cum H, scribant: sunt qui sine H. Porrò quod ad Adriam attinet, vide Strabonem li.5. & 7. Geographiæ, & Plinium lib.3.cap.16.
DOMITIA Paulina supradicti Ælij Adriani uxor, Imperatorisque Adriani mater fuit. erat hæc Gadibus orta. Vide Ælium Spartianum.

page.notes: The two medallions are pictures; only their legends are transcribed, as lines. The first legend runs off the edge of the medallion, so its end is uncertain. The ornament block at the foot has no text. The gathering signature "Ccc 3" is printed at the right below the text. A faint mark at the very bottom centre of the page is not text and is left out.
